html:
SMTO-SCH-0017 — This schedule has no future dates left

GUID: f700e54a-7572-4caa-b13b-7c431997e569
Slug: schedule-exhausted
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Based on its repeat pattern, start date and end setting, this schedule would never run again. SMTO didn't save it, so nothing will run from it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, select Edit, and look at Ends. If it is On date with a past date, pick a later date or choose Never. An end date that has already passed leaves no days for the schedule to run.
  2. If Ends is set to After a number of runs, raise that number or choose Never. A schedule that has already used up all its runs has nothing left to do.
  3. Check Starts, the repeat days and Time zone together, and make sure at least one matching day is in the future. A pattern like "the 31st of February" or a start after the end date never matches a real day.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and its card shows a future date under Next run.

If it still fails

  • Select New schedule and set up the timing from scratch. If that also fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the timing you wanted.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • This schedule has no remaining occurrences. Change its recurrence range or create a new schedule.

What this means

  • Calendar recurrence calculation yields no next occurrence for a new or reactivated/changed schedule. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Calendar recurrence calculation yields no next occurrence for a new or reactivated/changed schedule.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect start/end/count limits and the current clock against the recurrence preview.

How to fix it

  • next_calendar() returned no next occurrence for the calendar recurrence (on create, or on an update that changes recurrence, timezone, schedule_type or sets status active). Check recurrence.start_date, end (until date or count) and the weekday/month pattern against the schedule timezone, then widen the range or create a new schedule.
  • Change the recurrence range deliberately or create a new schedule with the intended next occurrence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate intended range has a valid next occurrence.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
